refs.quote: Diovan ® is indicated for the treatment of hypertension, to lower blood pressure in adults and pediatric patients one year of age and older. Lowering blood pressure reduces the risk of fatal and nonfatal cardiovascular events, primarily strokes and myocardial infarctions.

The recommended starting dose of Diovan is 80 mg or 160 mg once daily when used as monotherapy in patients who are not volume-depleted. Patients requiring greater reductions may be started at the higher dose. Diovan may be used over a dose range of 80 mg to 320 mg daily, administered once a day.

dose.frequency: once daily (starting 80-160 mg once daily; range 80-320 mg once daily)

regimens.dose_text: Starting dose 80 mg or 160 mg PO once daily; dose range 80 mg to 320 mg once daily. May add a diuretic or increase up to 320 mg once daily.

regimens.indication: Hypertension — Pediatric Patients (1 to 16 years of age)

refs.quote: 1 to 16 Years of Age The usual recommended starting dose is 1 mg/kg once daily (up to 40 mg total). A higher starting dose of 2 mg/kg may be considered in selected cases when a greater reduction of blood pressure is needed. The dosage should be adjusted according to blood pressure response and tolerability, up to a maximum dose of 4 mg/kg once daily (maximum daily dose 160 mg).

dose.frequency: once daily (range 1 to 4 mg/kg once daily)

regimens.dose_text: Starting dose 1 mg/kg PO once daily (up to 40 mg total; 2 mg/kg may be considered if greater BP reduction needed); adjust up to maximum 4 mg/kg once daily (max 160 mg/day). Not recommended in children < 1 year. Note: oral suspension has 60% higher AUC than tablets.

refs.quote: Diovan is indicated to reduce the risk of hospitalization for heart failure in adult patients with heart failure (NYHA class II-IV).

The recommended starting dose of Diovan is 40 mg twice daily. Uptitrate to 80 mg and 160 mg twice daily or to the highest dose tolerated by the patient. Consider reducing the dose of concomitant diuretics. The maximum daily dose administered in clinical trials is 320 mg in divided doses.

dose.frequency: twice daily (uptitrate to 80-160 mg twice daily as tolerated)

regimens.dose_text: Starting dose 40 mg PO twice daily; uptitrate to 80 mg and 160 mg twice daily or highest tolerated dose (max 320 mg/day in divided doses).

regimens.indication: Post-Myocardial Infarction (Clinically Stable Adults with LV Failure or LV Dysfunction)

refs.quote: In clinically stable adult patients with left ventricular failure or left ventricular dysfunction following myocardial infarction, Diovan is indicated to reduce the risk of cardiovascular mortality [see Clinical Studies (14.3)] .

Diovan may be initiated as early as 12 hours after a myocardial infarction. The recommended starting dose of Diovan is 20 mg twice daily. Patients may be uptitrated within 7 days to 40 mg twice daily, with subsequent titrations to a target maintenance dose of 160 mg twice daily, as tolerated by the patient.

dose.frequency: twice daily (uptitrate within 7 days to 40 mg BID, target 160 mg BID)

regimens.dose_text: Initiate as early as 12 hours post-MI at 20 mg PO twice daily; uptitrate within 7 days to 40 mg twice daily, then to target maintenance dose of 160 mg twice daily as tolerated.

refs.quote: Hypersensitivity: Angioedema has been reported. Some of these patients previously experienced angioedema with other drugs, including ACE inhibitors. Diovan should not be re-administered to patients who have had angioedema.
Creatinine: In heart failure trials, greater than 50% increases in creatinine were observed in 3.9% of Diovan-treated patients compared to 0.9% of placebo-treated patients.

mechanism_of_action.value: Nonpeptide, orally active angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) that selectively blocks binding of angiotensin II to the AT1 receptor (~20,000-fold greater affinity for AT1 than AT2) in vascular smooth muscle and the adrenal gland, inhibiting vasoconstriction and aldosterone secretion without inhibiting ACE (kininase II).

In vitro metabolism studies involving recombinant CYP 450 enzymes indicated that the CYP 2C9 isoenzyme is responsible for the formation of valeryl-4-hydroxy valsartan. Valsartan does not inhibit CYP 450 isozymes at clinically relevant concentrations.

enzyme_profile.note: Primary metabolite (~9% of dose) formed via CYP2C9; ~83% recovered in feces and ~13% in urine mainly as unchanged drug. Substrate of hepatic transporters OATP1B1 and MRP2.

value.drug_or_class: Aliskiren / Dual RAS Blockade (ACE Inhibitors, ARBs)
value.effect: Dual blockade of the RAS is associated with increased risks of hypotension, hyperkalemia, and changes in renal function (including acute renal failure) compared to monotherapy.
value.management: Do not coadminister aliskiren with Diovan in patients with diabetes. Avoid use of aliskiren in patients with GFR < 60 mL/min, and in general avoid combined use of RAS inhibitors.

refs.locator: 7.3 Dual Blockade of the Renin-Angiotensin System (RAS)
refs.quote: In general, avoid combined use of RAS inhibitors. Closely monitor blood pressure, renal function and electrolytes in patients on Diovan and other agents that affect the RAS. Do not coadminister aliskiren with Diovan in patients with diabetes. Avoid use of aliskiren with Diovan in patients with renal impairment (GFR < 60 mL/min).

value.drug_or_class: Potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, salt substitutes, heparin
value.effect: May lead to increases in serum potassium, and in heart failure patients, increases in serum creatinine.
value.management: If co-medication is considered necessary, monitoring of serum potassium is advisable.

refs.quote: Concomitant use of valsartan with other agents that block the renin-angiotensin system, potassium-sparing diuretics (e.g., spironolactone, triamterene, amiloride), potassium supplements, salt substitutes containing potassium or other drugs that may increase potassium levels (e.g., heparin) may lead to increases in serum potassium and in heart failure patients to increases in serum creatinine.

value.effect: May result in deterioration of renal function (including possible acute renal failure) in elderly, volume-depleted, or renally impaired patients; antihypertensive effect may be attenuated.
value.management: Monitor renal function periodically in patients receiving valsartan and NSAID therapy.

refs.locator: 7.2 Non-Steroidal Anti-Inflammatory Agents Including Selective Cyclooxygenase-2 Inhibitors (COX-2 Inhibitors)
refs.quote: coadministration of NSAIDs, including selective COX-2 inhibitors, with angiotensin II receptor antagonists, including valsartan, may result in deterioration of renal function, including possible acute renal failure. These effects are usually reversible. Monitor renal function periodically in patients receiving valsartan and NSAID therapy.

value.effect: Increases in serum lithium concentrations and lithium toxicity have been reported during concomitant administration.
value.management: Monitor serum lithium levels during concomitant use.

refs.quote: Increases in serum lithium concentrations and lithium toxicity have been reported during concomitant administration of lithium with angiotensin II receptor antagonists. Monitor serum lithium levels during concomitant use.

value.drug_or_class: OATP1B1 or MRP2 Inhibitors (e.g., rifampin, cyclosporine, ritonavir)
value.effect: Valsartan is a substrate of OATP1B1 and MRP2; coadministration of inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to valsartan.
value.management: Monitor blood pressure and clinical response if coadministered with potent OATP1B1 or MRP2 inhibitors.

refs.quote: The results from an in vitro study with human liver tissue indicate that valsartan is a substrate of the hepatic uptake transporter OATP1B1 and the hepatic efflux transporter MRP2. Coadministration of inhibitors of the uptake transporter (rifampin, cyclosporine) or efflux transporter (ritonavir) may increase the systemic exposure to valsartan.

There is no information regarding the presence of Diovan in human milk, the effects on the breastfed infant, or the effects on milk production. Diovan is present in rat milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in breastfed infants from exposure to valsartan, advise a nursing woman that breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment with Diovan.
